title: Elastic Runway Scorer and Deferred Scope Catalog
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: We lack a lightweight, auditable scoring mechanism to decide which initiatives are eligible for mid-cycle deferral or partial trim when runway tightens. This causes ad-hoc scope cuts, repeated rework across PM/Eng/Design, and poor signals for OKR owners. Goal: Build an "Elastic Runway Scorer" (ERS) and a Deferred Scope Catalog (DSC) so PMs can quickly score initiatives against common fiscal and operational criteria and produce an ordered, rationale-backed list of scope candidates to defer or reduce.
background: Over the last three cycles we've observed at least five mid-cycle rebalances where scope decisions were made in Slack threads and weekly PM syncs; downstream work in Eng and Design was often cancelled with limited context. Engineering reported duplicated ramp costs and dropped infra changes that introduced regressions. The ERS is intended to standardize decisions, speed tradeoffs, and provide a paper trail for stakeholders and OKR owners.
proposed_solution: 1) Define a 6-factor scoring rubric (customer value, OKR fit, cross-team dependencies, implementation effort, risk/regulatory blockers, opportunity cost). 2) Build a lightweight spreadsheet + template in Confluence for derivation and narrative. 3) Add a Console widget mockup (read-only) to surface the highest-ranked deferred items per initiative. 4) Run a 2-week pilot across three initiatives during Cycle 2026-W11 to validate scoring thresholds and handoff rituals.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Week 1): Finalize rubric and Confluence template; training doc for PMs. Phase 2 (Week 2): Pilot with Growth, Runtime, and Console initiatives; collect time-to-decision and stakeholder feedback. Phase 3 (Week 4): Incorporate feedback, ship a light 'deferred scope' YAML export for Eng trackers and add a Console read-only card for leadership. Phase 4 (Post-cycle): Formalize into the Cycle Playbook and add to planning rituals.
acceptance_criteria: Rubric defined and published in Confluence with worked examples
Three pilot initiatives scored and outcomes recorded
Pilot feedback summary with suggested threshold for automatic escalate vs manual review
Deferred Scope Catalog entries exported as YAML/CSV and consumed by at least one ENG tracker
open_questions: What minimum score threshold should trigger an automatic deferral recommendation vs. require a cross-functional review?
How do we account for third-party or legal blockers in the score (e.g., compliance work that cannot be deferred)?
Who owns the final sign-off for pipeline-level decommits in large initiatives (PM vs. Engineering Director)?
decisions: Use 0-5 numeric scale per factor; total score normalized to 0-30
Compliance/legal blockers are a veto flag (binary) and recorded in the DSC
Pilot will use Confluence + a canonical Google Sheet; engineering integration is YAML export only (no product changes to trackers yet)
